checks.detail: toned.md conforms to the CSA template: header block, Executive Summary, Current Microsoft Cloud Security Posture (Posture Summary, Key Risk Themes, Domain Posture, Control Movement and Baseline Changes), Security Signal Review (Identity and Access, Endpoint and Vulnerabilities, Data Protection and Collaboration, Cloud Workload and Attack Path Exposure, AI Agents and Generative AI Usage, Detection and Operational Readiness), and Recommended Security Actions (Security Awareness, Active Recommendations, CIS Microsoft 365 Foundation Benchmark, Deferred Recommendations, Recommendation History with CIS and Advisory subsections). Every substantive domain section is conclusion-first with condition, quarter movement, evidence, significance, qualification, and recommended response (e.g., 'Identity is Team Daks' highest-priority domain because MFA coverage remains incomplete despite the Q3 score gain'; 'Data protection is a priority gap because the evidence cannot show that Team Daks' sensitive information is classified or protected by policy'). No section reproduces raw source data without a security significance statement; each domain table carries an 'Assessment interpretation' column. Movement is temporally anchored to Q3 with explicit statement that population-driven score movement is not policy change. Positive findings are calibrated (email malware/link credit explicitly not equivalent to impersonation protection); risk scope is bounded with 'unknown risk' framing for unassessed domains. Cross-signal synthesis groups authentication/privileged access, impersonation, information protection, external collaboration, and logging themes rather than listing isolated controls. Client-consultative voice leads with conclusions and interpretations; Microsoft/CIS/NIST inputs are supporting. The Security Awareness subsection is exempt from conclusion-first but remains compliant with substance freeze and banned-pattern checks.

Token diff between draft.md and toned.md yields exactly three differences, all recorded in tone-changes.json and none introducing or altering a factual token: (1) 'Data is the weakest category' → 'the Data category is the weakest'; (2) 'Use the latter for custom policy scope and exceptions' → 'Use Conditional Access for custom policy scope and exceptions' (same referent); (3) 'Q2026 3 - Audit controls are uncredited' → '2026 Q3 - Audit controls are uncredited' (quarter-label typo fix). All numbers (37.49%, 36.72%, 36.61%, 48.33%, 44.42%, 43.85%, 100.48/268, 46.08%, 55.54%, 1.99/9, 2.14/9, 9.41/10, 7.93/8, 8/8, 0.15, 0.07, 3.91, 4.48, 0.77, 0.88, 101/131, 103/130, 2.06/9, 1.85/9, 0/8, 0/5, 0/2, 0/1, 0/3, 0/7, 4/4, 1/1, 3/3, 0/1, 9/9, 8/8, 5/5, 6/6, 3/3, 1/1), dates (2023.Q3, 2026.Q1, 2026.Q3, 2026 Q3, Q1–Q3 2026, Q1–Q2 2026), control titles, CIS references (5.2.2.1, 5.2.2.2, 5.2.2.3, 5.1.5.1, 1.3.1, 7.2.1, 6.5.1, 2.1.7, 2.1.4, 2.1.5, 2.1.1, 6.2.1, 3.2.1, 3.3.1, 3.1.1, 6.1.2), NIST references (PR.AA-03, PR.AA-05, PR.PS-01, PR.PS-04, PR.DS-01, PR.DS-02, PR.DS-10, DE.CM-09, PR.AT-01, PR.AT-02), and recommendations appear unchanged in toned.md.

Semantic inventory matches. All entities (Team Daks, Danish Dhedi, Danny George), measurements, findings (incomplete MFA coverage, legacy-auth regression, uncredited impersonation protections, Data 0%, uncredited audit controls, unassessed endpoint/vulnerability/cloud-workload/AI domains), and recommendations (priorities 0–5, CIS benchmark rows, Deferred Recommendations, Recommendation History) present in draft.md are present in toned.md with identical client-facing meaning, and vice versa. No finding dropped or merged with changed scope; no recommendation strength upgraded or downgraded; no metric restated on a different basis; no cause/effect claim re-attributed. The three edits are lexical/terminological and preserve meaning.

tone-changes.json validates against tone-changes.schema.json: top-level changes, tables_reviewed, observations present, certifiable=true. Each of the three recorded edits carries location, before, after, style_marker (plain_language, terminology, spelling), reason, assessment_function (evidence_interpretation, recommendation_traceability, recommendation_traceability), and facts_changed=false. Every table in draft.md is represented in tables_reviewed: Domain Posture (8 rows), Identity control-evidence (5), Endpoint Exposure Level (3), Endpoint control-evidence (5), Data Protection control-evidence (5), Cloud Workload control-evidence (5), AI control-evidence (5), Active Recommendations (6), CIS Foundation Benchmark (4), Recommendation History CIS (1), Recommendation History Advisory (2). Table edits match tone-changes.json row by row (Active Recommendations rows 0 and 4 edited; all others unchanged). observations entries cite concrete locations. assessment_function set {evidence_interpretation, recommendation_traceability} is not exclusively template_structure/professional_tone, so the coverage rule is satisfied.

run-state.json shows punchouts.A_missing_content.triggered=false and punchouts.E_loop_exhaustion.triggered=false, so no two-key closure is required. certifiable=true with non_certifiable_reasons=[]. No bypass_attempt recorded. tone-changes.json certifiable=true. No self-granted approval present.

toned.md contains no PHI/PII tied to findings, no credentials/secrets/keys/tokens, no harness internals, audit-log paths, agent prompts, or debugging notes, and no tenant data from a client other than the report subject. Only the report-header contacts Danish Dhedi (Prepared For) and Danny George (Prepared By) appear, which the template requires and which are not tied to findings.
No failing check; g5-judgment.md is not required for this run.

findings.detail: Only three edits recorded, all lexical/terminological; the assessment_function set is {evidence_interpretation, recommendation_traceability}. This satisfies the change-accountability coverage rule (not exclusively template_structure/professional_tone) and the draft was already assessment-quality, so toned.md meets the G5 quality criteria without a larger analytical rewrite.
